guideTitle: 5 Best Portable Chargers With Wall Plugs (2026)
metaTitle: Best Portable Chargers With Wall Plugs (2026)
metaDescription: Five portable chargers with built-in wall plugs compared on capacity, fast charging, cable design, and size, so you can skip the extra adapter.
introParagraphs: A portable charger with a built-in wall plug does two jobs in one body, since it works as a power bank on the go and plugs straight into an outlet to recharge itself. That removes an adapter from your bag and a step from your routine. The five picks here range from the TESSAN at 30W to the citicr at 20000mAh.

Capacity and design vary. The citicr carries 20000mAh with a 90 degree foldable plug, the FOCHEW offers 13800mAh, and the Coowisty, TESSAN, and LUCKYFELLOW are 10000mAh. The LUCKYFELLOW is also magnetic and can charge an Apple Watch, while the Coowisty fits four cable types into a slim body.

We evaluated these on product specs and buyer feedback, focusing on plug design, charging speed, capacity, and size. A universal travel adapter that was in the original candidate list was removed because it is not a power bank. The sections below rank the five and explain how to choose.

products.name: TESSAN 10000mAh 3-in-1 Power Bank With Wall Plug
products.description:
The TESSAN is a three-in-one device that works as a wall charger, a power bank, and a cable holder. It has a foldable AC plug, a built-in USB-C cable rated at 30W that doubles as a lanyard, and an additional USB-C port. Two-way 30W charging means it can quickly top up a phone or recharge itself.

The listing carries an honest capacity note, explaining that the 10000mAh total is built from two 5000mAh cells and that the 5000mAh marking on the unit refers to a single cell. That kind of transparency is rare and helpful. The tradeoff is that the built-in cable cannot be replaced, and the feature mix is less broad than the Coowisty.

It works well as a simple desk-to-bag charger. Compared with the citicr, it has half the capacity but a faster 30W path. Compared with the FOCHEW, it is simpler but better suited to USB-C phones.
products.bestFor: USB-C phone owners who want fast charging and a plug in one slim unit.
pros: Built-in USB-C cable doubles as a lanyard

products.name: citicr 20000mAh PD20W Power Bank With Wall Plug
products.description:
The citicr is the capacity leader here at 20000mAh, which the maker says gives three to five full phone charges. It combines a dedicated PD20W Type-C output and a 22.5W path, and claims a phone can reach 60 percent in half an hour. The AC plug folds at 90 degrees, so it sits flat when stored.

Built-in cables remove the need for a separate cord, which helps in a travel bag. The tradeoff is size, since 20000mAh is about 74 Wh and noticeably heavier than the 10000mAh models. That is still inside the common 100 Wh carry-on limit, so it can fly.

It suits long trips or a household with several devices. Compared with the TESSAN, it has double the energy but less peak power. Compared with the Coowisty, it is larger and heavier but stretches much further between recharges.
products.bestFor: Long trips and heavy users who want a wall-plug charger with big capacity.
pros: 20000mAh gives three to five phone charges
About 74 Wh stays within carry-on rules

products.name: Coowisty 10000mAh Power Bank With Wall Plug

specList.label: Cables
specList.value: USB-C plus Micro and iPhone, 2 ports

products.description:
The Coowisty combines a foldable wall plug with two built-in cables and two ports, plus an LED display that shows the charge. It measures 6 x 2.7 x 0.7 inches and weighs 8 oz, which is slim for a plug-equipped bank. The foldable plug saves space in a bag.

It supports pass-through charging, so you can recharge it from the wall while it charges your phone. That is useful at an airport gate with only one outlet. The tradeoff is that the 10000mAh capacity is modest compared with the citicr, and the built-in cables are fixed.

The LED display is a real help because you see exactly how much is left. Compared with the TESSAN, it offers more cable variety but lacks the 30W speed. Compared with the FOCHEW, it is lighter on capacity but easier to pocket.
products.bestFor: Travelers who want a slim plug-in bank with a clear display.

products.name: FOCHEW 13800mAh Power Bank With Wall Plug
products.description:
The FOCHEW sits between the 10000mAh models and the citicr with 13800mAh of capacity. It has a built-in Type-C cable, another cable for iPhone, and an AC wall plug, plus a Type-C and USB-A output. The listing emphasizes wide compatibility with recent iPhones.

Four outputs let two people charge at once, which suits a couple. The tradeoff is that the maker publishes fewer details about wattage, so speed is harder to compare. Like the others, the built-in cables are fixed.

It makes sense for a mixed household that has an iPhone and a USB-C device. Compared with the Coowisty, it has more capacity but no display. Compared with the TESSAN, it supports Lightning but gives up the 30W path.
products.bestFor: Mixed iPhone and Android households that want a plug and extra capacity.
pros: 13800mAh sits between small and large banks

products.name: LUCKYFELLOW 10000mAh Magnetic Power Bank With Wall Plug
products.description:
The LUCKYFELLOW is the only magnetic pick with a wall plug, and it can also charge an Apple Watch. It uses N52 magnets with a precise alignment system for phones and watches. Three built-in cables and an AC plug mean it can recharge two ways.

The Apple Watch feature has a quirk, as the listing advises removing the watch band if the watch will not charge steadily. That is a small usability wrinkle. Magnetic charging is also slower than a cable, so it is better for steady top-ups.

It suits Apple users who want one device to cover phone and watch. Compared with the Coowisty, it is more specialized and less slim. Compared with the TESSAN, it offers magnetism but not 30W.
products.bestFor: Apple users who want a magnetic bank that also charges a watch and plugs into a wall.
cons: Wireless charging is slower than a cable
Apple Watch charging needs the band removed sometimes

buyingCriteria.explanation: A foldable plug is what makes this category practical, since a fixed prong tears at pockets. The citicr has a 90 degree fold and the Coowisty and TESSAN fold flat. Check that the plug retracts fully and locks. Outlet recess and wall plate shape can also block bulky plugs.

Compare watt-hours rather than milliamp hours, where Wh equals mAh divided by 1000 times about 3.6 to 3.7 volts. The 20000mAh citicr is about 74 Wh, the FOCHEW about 51 Wh, and the 10000mAh models about 37 Wh. All are below the 100 Wh carry-on limit. Usable output is roughly 77 to 83 percent of the rating.

USB-C Power Delivery spans 18 to 100W while typical USB-A ports give only 5 to 12W. The TESSAN reaches 30W, the citicr offers PD20W and 22.5W, and the others are slower. If your phone supports fast charging, choose at least 20W. Slow banks work but make long waits.

Some listings overstate capacity. The TESSAN explains that its 10000mAh total is two 5000mAh cells, which helps buyers understand the markings. Check for a printed Wh rating, since security may confiscate banks without one. Choose brands that explain their numbers.

Built-in cables help only if they match your devices. The FOCHEW and LUCKYFELLOW include iPhone connectors, while the TESSAN is USB-C only. Fixed cables cannot be replaced if damaged. Match connectors to what you own.
A plug adds thickness. The Coowisty is 0.7 inches thick and 8 oz, which is a sensible limit for a bag. Heavier banks like the citicr suit a backpack. Choose the lightest unit that covers your trip.

howWeEvaluated.title: Plug and portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at plug folding, thickness, and weight, from the Coowisty's 0.7 inches to the larger citicr. A plug that sticks out damages bags. We favored flat folds. The strongest pick folded cleanly and stayed slim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated output, from the TESSAN's 30W to the citicr's PD20W and 22.5W. Speed matters most for a nearly empty phone. We treated maker figures as claims rather than measurements. The fastest wired path led our ranking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared capacity and how clearly each listing explains it, with the TESSAN's cell note a highlight. Usable energy is below the printed number. We favored transparent listings. The citicr and TESSAN sit at opposite ends of capacity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cable compatibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at which cables are built in and which devices they serve. The FOCHEW and LUCKYFELLOW include iPhone connectors, while the TESSAN is USB-C. Fixed cables are a durability risk. We rewarded flexibility.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed relative price tier against features, with the TESSAN the lowest-cost pick and the citicr the premium one. We used product specs and buyer feedback rather than hands-on use. Safety marks and protections also counted.

rows: iPhone and USB-C in one home

cards.label: Slim 10000mAh
cards.text: The TESSAN, Coowisty, and LUCKYFELLOW are light and cover one to two refills. They suit daily carry. Recommended for commuters.

cards.label: High capacity
cards.text: The citicr and FOCHEW give more charges but weigh more. They suit trips and families. Recommended for travel.

howToChoose.note: Choose slim for daily use and high capacity for trips.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A bank under 100 Wh with pass-through charging and a plug that folds flat, so one outlet powers both bank and phone.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Coowisty supports pass-through and has a display, and the citicr at about 74 Wh still flies. Both suit travelers.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need several days of power, where the citicr earns its place. You also want a watch-friendly magnetic design, as the LUCKYFELLOW provides.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want fast charging and a plug at the lowest cost, where the TESSAN is enough.

faq.q: How do I choose between these wall-plug chargers?
faq.a: Start with capacity and phone type. The citicr gives the most energy, the TESSAN the fastest speed, and the LUCKYFELLOW adds magnets. Match the pick to your trips.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a charger with a wall plug?
faq.a: The TESSAN is the lowest-cost pick and still fast. The Coowisty and FOCHEW sit mid-range. The citicr costs more for its capacity.
Foldable plugs are designed for repeated folding, but they can loosen over time. Check that the plug locks. Handle it gently.

faq.q: Can I take these on a plane?
faq.a: Yes, in carry-on bags only. The citicr at about 74 Wh is under the common 100 Wh limit, and the 10000mAh models are about 37 Wh. Check your airline's rules.

faq.q: What does 10000mAh made of two 5000mAh cells mean?
faq.a: The TESSAN explains that its total capacity comes from two 5000mAh internal cells. The 5000mAh marking on the unit refers to one cell. The total is still 10000mAh.

faq.q: Can a wall-plug bank charge while plugged in?
faq.a: Many support pass-through charging, such as the Coowisty. That means the bank and phone charge together. Check the listing for this feature.
